en.old: Web hydration is an essential process in building interactive applications, and various tools and frameworks can optimize or ease it. Below you will find the most relevant categories of these solutions, along with a performance comparison that lets you analyze how effective they are.
en.new: Web hydration is an essential process in building interactive applications, and various tools and frameworks can optimize or ease it. Below you will find the most relevant categories of these solutions, along with a comparison of both approaches.

en.old: Solutions That Support Resumability
en.new: Resumability and Partial Hydration in Practice

en.old: As the need for more efficient solutions grows, some tools are starting to adopt resumability instead of traditional hydration. These include:
en.new: Qwik is the framework built around resumability: it pauses execution on the server and resumes it in the browser without hydrating the application. Other well-known tools do hydrate, and each one handles it in its own way:

en.old: : Squarely focused on performance optimization, this React framework facilitates state serialization and concentrates on loading pages on the server side, which minimizes the need for a heavy hydration process.
en.new: : It relies on React hydration. With Server Components in the App Router, the code of server components never reaches the browser and only client components hydrate.

en.old: : Unlike other frameworks, Svelte compiles code into highly efficient JavaScript, which removes the need to hydrate the DOM altogether and improves speed and user experience.
en.new: : It compiles components to JavaScript and hydrates as well. With SvelteKit the browser hydrates server-rendered HTML by default, and you can turn JavaScript off on pages that do not need it.

en.old: : With its philosophy of sending as little JavaScript as possible to the client, Astro lets developers choose static or dynamic components and manage interactivity without the usual hydration overhead.
en.new: : It applies partial hydration through islands. It renders static HTML and hydrates only the components you mark as interactive.
